correctness.rationale: For absorption on step T, the probability of no intervening reset is s^(T-1); the common factor s^-1 cancels in the renewal ratio A/(A+B). The tridiagonal inverse entries from site 7 to sites 1 and 15 have the respective unique path products and complementary block determinants R and L, divided by the same full determinant. Including each final boundary step gives B/A=C s^2 L/R. All killed blocks have spectral radius <1 by uniform positive escape probability in finitely many steps; their real determinants start at 1 and cannot vanish on [0,1]. Independently recomputed the two determinants by enumerating disjoint neighboring transpositions, not by the supplied continuant. At t=3/5,3/4,19/20,1 the exact signs of (L+tL')R-tLR' are +,-,+,-. Thus Q' has signs -,+,-,+; its nonzero analytic numerator ensures a strict minimum, maximum, minimum in the respective disjoint interior intervals, even with the last test at the endpoint. No root count beyond these three is needed.
residual_risks: This certifies at least three extrema, not exactly three, minimal chain size for three, or a bound over all chains.

value.rationale: An explicit, rational nearest-neighbor witness rules out a general two-turn classification in the inhomogeneous one-site model, advancing the published question about several reset extrema. It is a useful exact benchmark for further state-count or oscillation bounds, not merely a different parameter set displaying the already known two turns.
residual_risks: Counterexample to a uniform two-turn limit, not a general classification or extremum-location theorem.
